column1: # The patch queue against patches/BASE, one row per patch; checked by tools/moira_queue.py check.
# state: local|proposed|merged|dropped; relation of the upstream PR to the patch: identical|same-behaviour|partial|diverged
# repro: case of tools/dirk_moira/findings_repro.cpp; evidence: manual locators cited by the patch message, none, sst-only or inferred

column10: note

extends upstream readStatusRefill() (PR #43, merged in 863b8d02) to the expired DBcc and the trapping TRAPV; only with an emulated instruction cache, like the merged MOVE to SR/CCR; triage 2026-11-26: the discarded read of TRAPV is Moira's model (the tables give a trapping TRAPV the prefetches of TRAP #n); with an emulated cache that CACR disables the latch can serve the word where the no-cache columns count three prefetches, the property of merged PR #43; 2026-11-27: that latch hit is documented behaviour, not a defect (MC68030UM 11.6: the instruction-access figure is the average of both alignments rounded up; MC68020UM 1.6: the holding register serves the pipe with the cache disabled; 12.7.1: condition-code operations request no refill), so no latch fix is owed; the DBcc half is prepared alone as branch dbcc-expired-refill (MC68030UM 12.7.1 places the speculative refill at the branch target, the core reads DBcc+4); 2026-11-27: the DBcc half proposed as PR #52 (branch dbcc-expired-refill); upstream the discarded read follows CYCLES_68020(10), so no clock changes, where this patch reads before; the TRAPV half stays local
host interface for save states, not CPU behaviour
the LC II slot-probe recovery ran 28.8 million times without it; patch 4 (context) and patch 9 depend on it; triage 2026-11-26: a design question for discussion #36 before any PR

a host BusError escaped to the caller; reset() halts on a BusError or an AddressError (8.1.1); since 2026-11-26 a fault on the trace frame takes the bus error exception through processException(), like the interrupt path, and only a second fault halts (7.5.4 lists bus error, address error and reset, not trace); depends textually on patch 3 (context line); only the 68030 manual was read for a change that reaches every model; the SR that bus error frame stacks is [F] (moira_rules_test traceFrameFault); 2026-11-27: the 68000 and 68020/68030 manuals were read (they support taking the bus error), MC68040UM 7.6.3 and Figures 8-1, 8-4 lean toward a halt on any fault during exception processing, interrupts included, so the 68040 half is [F]; prepared upstream as branches reset-bus-fault and trace-frame-fault, which add what this patch lacks (debugger reset and didResetCPU() before the halt, an odd trace vector, the 68000 I/N bit)

debugger interface, not CPU behaviour; a host built with MOIRA_VIRTUAL_API=false must define the new delegate; program is false for a plain program read (jumpToVector()); triage 2026-11-26: an interface question for discussion #36
no effect on upstream, where jumpToVector() calls catchpointMatches() without reading CHECK_CP; the bit is read by src/MoiraCompat.h; never a PR

trapVector() takes a nonmaskable mask for integer destinations; since 2026-11-26 a following FSAVE stores the opclass 011 SNAN/OPERR frame of Table 9-16 (CMDREG1B, ETEMP, STAG, E1, T) in the unimplemented instruction layout: with an idle frame the FPSP handler of the Quadra 605 ROM stored a ROM address for a signaling NaN (q605_fpsp_moveout_etalon runs that handler); [F] which of the $30 and $60 frames the 68040 stacks there; the largest negative integer (9.7.3.2) and the nonmaskable overflow (9.7.4.2) are not covered; triage 2026-11-26: belongs with upstream's 68040 state frames, a question for discussion #36
message cites no manual passage; the restart contract is Moira's own
extends patch 3's completed-cycle record; depends semantically on patch 11 (the size it reports); triage 2026-11-26: local until a 68030 capture on a 16-bit port

the 68020 frame stacked 0 at SP+$18; rebased on PR #42: the frame takes frame.ssw (upstream) and the data output buffer; 2026-11-27: proposed as PR #51 (branch 68020-data-output-buffer), with a known difference for frame.dob in ExceptionUAE020

read from MC68020UM 6.2.1, MC68030UM 8.2.1-8.2.2 and MC68040UM 8.4.6.2 together; settled by a 68030 on a 16-bit port; rebased on PR #42: completeBusError(e, addr, instructionFetch) keeps upstream instructionFetch

a handler completing WB3 wrote two bytes too far; after a translation the FA was the physical address (moira_rules_test hostBusErrorFaultAddressIsLogical040; WinUAE @ Hatari e77819f7 stacks the physical one, the manual overrules it); depends on patch 11 (completeBusError(e, addr, ...)) and textually on patch 5; a host /BERR on a translated instruction fetch also changes from the physical to the logical address (8.4.6.7); triage 2026-11-26: proposable once rebased alone; 2026-11-27: proposed as PR #53 (branch 68040-fault-address), written alone on his master, without the split helpers of patch 9
not upstreamable as written: evidence is SingleStepTests 68000/v1 only
not upstreamable: evidence is SingleStepTests 68000/v1 only (grade D); M68000PRM calls N and Z undefined on overflow

changes cycles only where the instruction cache is not emulated, the 68LC040/68040 (+4 Moira cycles on the discarded refill word of MOVE to SR/CCR, an expired DBcc, a taken TRAPV); nothing on a 68020/68030 whose instruction cache is emulated (a MOIRA_EMULATE_ICACHE=false build changes too); 040 half [F] until the port width/cadence is recalibrated: the 68040 wrappers answer the 16-bit dsack() (src/Moira040Cpu.h) that MC68040UM 7.2 contradicts, a speed setting tuned with cacheBoost_; depends on patch 1 for the DBcc and TRAPV cases; the tables show the extra prefetch for MOVE to SR and the expired DBcc only, not for MOVE to CCR nor TRAPV; triage 2026-11-26: never a PR

format 9 frame: scan PC at +2, instruction address at +8; RTE unchanged (reloads +2); shares the move-out block of execFMove with patch 7 (its comment line and context); reverses the 2026-11-24 deferred reading; the 68882 re-takes the exception after a handler without FSAVE (MC68881UM 7.5.4.2, Figure 7-34), the core takes it once: a known divergence for such a handler only; WinUAE (Hatari e77819f7) stacks format 3 instead; textual context from patches 7 and 10 (does not apply alone); since 2026-11-26 a traced FMOVE keeps its trace event past the exception, taken before the handler's first instruction as after a TRAP (MC68030UM 8.1.7, Table 8-6; the point is [F]: the after-RTE reading has MC68030UM 10.4.4, 10.4.19, 10.5.2.5 and 8.1.4 for it; fpu_sanity moveOutTraced); prepared upstream as branch 6888x-fmove-out-mid-instruction; a PR must update upstream's FpuExecTests '68882' subcase

the 68040 keeps patch 7's rule (its Table 9-11 and 9.7.3.2 disagree on an SNAN source); two oracle vectors that set OPERR on FMOVE.W are listed in tests/sst68030.known; triage 2026-11-26: contested, MC68881UM 4.5.4.2 read with Table 6-2 gives SNAN and OPERR together with the SNAN trap disabled (upstream's behaviour), and MC68040UM Table 9-11 has Table 6-2's wording, so the 6888x/68040 split has no manual ground; [F] until a 68881/68882 capture, not a PR

a host /BERR on a descriptor read escaped translate(): the 68040 SSW lacked ATC and the 68030 frame carried the descriptor address; translate() ends the walk like an invalid descriptor (nonresident 68040 entry, 68030 entry with B); PTEST and PLOAD walks unchanged (moira_rules_test tableSearchBusError040, tableSearchBusError030); triage 2026-11-26: first PR candidate; a host custom frame (BusError::custom) is thrown on unmodified since 2026-11-26 (moira_rules_test tableSearchCustomFrame); a PR must state that the public mmu.translate() and a /BERR on the U/M write-back change too; no reproducer on the unmodified tree yet; 2026-11-27: proposed as PR #50 (branch mmu-table-search-bus-error); PTEST and PLOAD walks left for a follow-up

the second part of a misaligned access crossing pages went to phys + 2 (or phys + 1): wrong physical page under a non-contiguous mapping, no fault on an invalid second page; the 68040 stacks MA and the first byte, the 68030 frame (second page logical address, original size) is [F]; both pages are translated before the first bus cycle, so MC68040UM 4.1's double access to the first page is not modelled; only an access past a 256-byte boundary takes the second lookup (moira_rules_test misalignedAccessAcrossPages, misalignedAccessUnchangedPaths); depends on patch 12 (the phys/logical split); readAcross() and writeAcross() split like the misaligned path of readBus() (the 68020 core charges no cycle per data bus cycle, SYNC() is empty there); triage 2026-11-26: a question for discussion #36 before a PR

reproduced on unmodified bf98107f (findings_repro case 6: SSW without RM, and 14 bus errors where a handler that emulated TAS and cleared DF expects one); RM on the read and the write cycle of TAS, CAS, CAS2 (68020, 68030), not on the address computation; RTE with RM set and DF clear continues at the end captured at the fault, kept in the frame's internal register at $1C; depends textually on patch 3 (the RTE block that reads the SSW); the 68040 LK bit is left for its own patch; upstream ExceptionUAE020 compares only the SR, PC, format word and fault address of 68020 frames (ExceptionRunner::description() @ bf98107f), so RM and $1C do not differ there; his Tests/Unit not yet run on this patch; candidate for a PR after the owner reviews the text
